content.thinking:
I'm checking how to word the impact on customers without giving any count. "Many more" reads like a sizing term, so I'll avoid it and describe the purchases that were held on the newer card but not on the older ones.

I'm settling on wording that says the held purchases were flagged for fraud review more often than on the older cards, without putting a number on it. For the cost, the figure is still an estimate Argus owns, and no one was paged. The fix is held to the older graphics cards, confirmed and still in place, with automatic sync turned off, and a proposed fix is open as a draft but hasn't been run. I'll also leave out any specific identifiers and just say the older graphics cards. The duration is a placeholder I still need to fill in, and I'll avoid calling it brief.

input.overview: For {duration}, some io-shop customers had their purchases held for fraud review when they should not have been. The affected customers were the ones whose purchases went through one copy of the shop's service that had started on a newer kind of graphics card. On that card, the fraud check likely did its arithmetic less precisely, so that copy held more purchases than the copies running on the older cards. Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. To end it, Argus kept the shop's service on the older graphics cards only. That change is confirmed and still in place, and automatic syncing has been left off so it is not undone. Argus has also proposed a permanent fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied yet.
